title: Effect of tracheal antimicrobial peptide on the development of Mannheimia haemolytica pneumonia in cattle

what_it_measured.text: The MIC was determined as the minimum final concentration of TAP that resulted in no bacterial growth on the blood agar plates.

The lung: heart weight ratio was intended as an objective estimate of the amount of edema and cellular exudate filling the airspaces of the lung; heart weight was used as an estimate of body size because body weight varies with the amount of rumen fill.

dose.text: In the first two pairs of calves, 1 mg of TAP in 2 mL water was administered by aerosol 3 times (3 mg total).

The last 4 pairs of calves were given a larger TAP dose of 4 mg in 2 mL water by aerosol and 1 mg in 2 mL water by bilateral intranasal mist at each of the 3 treatments (15 mg total) using an atomizer device (MED-RX, Benlan Inc., Oakville, ON).

route.text: The last 4 pairs of calves were given a larger TAP dose of 4 mg in 2 mL water by aerosol and 1 mg in 2 mL water by bilateral intranasal mist at each of the 3 treatments (15 mg total) using an atomizer device (MED-RX, Benlan Inc., Oakville, ON).

endpoint.text: Next, calves were challenged with M. haemolytica and the effect of synthetic TAP on bacterial infection and pneumonia was evaluated.

Bactericidal activity of oxidized and non-oxidized TAP To determine if the three disulphide bonds in oxidized TAP affected the antibacterial properties of the peptide, the bactericidal activity of synthetic oxidized and non-oxidized TAP was measured against M. haemolytica B158 [5].

The presence of M. haemolytica in the lung was not significantly different between water-treated and TAP-treated calves, when assessed as the lobe with the maximum number of bacteria isolated (P = 0.49, paired t test) or as the mean for all lobes (P = 0.49, paired t test, log-transformed data).

reported_results.text: At concentrations of 3.12 and 6.25 μg/mL, non-oxidized TAP killed 96% and 99% of bacteria compared with 17% and 86% killing by oxidized TAP, respectively.
The effects of TAP, oxidation status, and their interaction were all significant (P<0.001, 2-way ANOVA; Fig 1).
This effect was significant with 25% BALF in 6.5 μg/mL TAP (50% inhibition of bactericidal activity), but not with lower or higher BALF concentrations.
Addition of 1.25% serum resulted in 49% inhibition of the bactericidal activity of 6.5 mM TAP, and 2.5% serum increased bacterial numbers by 7% (Fig 8B).
The addition of serum to TAP significantly increased the survival of M. haemolytica (P<0.0001, 2-way ANOVA, n = 3 technical replicates per group).
The addition of sodium chloride to TAP significantly increased the survival of M. haemolytica (P<0.0001, 2-way ANOVA, n = 3 technical replicates per group).
